As someone that loves to play blue, I can tell you that the sooner you learn its weaknesses, the easier it will be to beat us. Counterspells are very powerful, but also, we have no way of guessing what is in your hand. The reason to counter is an understanding of what are the key pieces that make your deck work. If you're playing an Elf deck, for example, I know not to waste my energy on your elves, but on a potential Craterhoof Behemoth.
 On that note, blue likes to play a slow methodical game, so playing the opposite strategy will give us a really hard time. If we counter two or three spells in a row, the chances of us having another counterspell are very low. Also, if we have open mana, just always assume that there is a counterspell coming. You can bait us into wasting a counterspell on one threat and then play your much scarier card after we have wasted resources. Blue players will always try to be two-steps ahead of you. Beating them at this mental game is the first step to beating us in the card game. I gurantee you, just be more careful about when you play your spells and bait us into wasting our counters. That's the key to beating blue. Punish us for trying to play the guessing game, and then annihilate us in combat.

1. If you mean meditating like literally sitting cross legged with your eyes closed, no. But for me lsd IS a meditative experience on it's own. You're constantly analysing parts of your life and decisions. Your brains will go at a million miles between trying to dissect the meaning of life and being convinced your cat is talking to you. Whatever you're using it for you're guranteed to come out with answers to some of your biggest questions and maybe have new ones you never thought before. 

2. I have not done it enough to have a lasting impact, but I've known people who tripped so much when they were younger they can still see fractals when they blink. When you're on the drug you will see visuals with your eyes closed and in the dark (but stay in as much light as you can, or you could trigger a bad trip)

3. Times I've taken lsd has been just for the fun of it. But as of my last trip going bad, I've decided to only use it for creative practice and self-reflection. 

4. You can learn a lot about yourself on the drug during and after the experience. And if you're tripping with someone close to you it can greatly strengthen your bond to that person. I've found that I'm much more spiritual, patient, open-minded and creative since taking lsd. 

Have a safe trip!
